messages: maya.kapoor: Heads up — noticed something odd in the admin audit UI during routine checks. A recent audit entry shows raw HTML in the role_description field and it rendered in the browser. maya.kapoor: PoC snippet from DB: `INSERT INTO audit_entries (actor, action, role_description) VALUES ('ext-integration', 'role.create', '')` — it actually executed when I opened /admin/audit nate.choi: yikes. can you repro on staging? or is this in prod only? maya.kapoor: repros on prod-staging and prod. staging had same entry from an integration test. prod has a couple entries that render. sec_oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (priority: high) — team eng-security notified. emily.ross: nice catch. immediate mitigation: hide admin audit rendering (render as plain text) and disable any markdown/html rendering in the audit UI. @frontend-eng can you flip the flag and ship a quick patch? frontend-eng: on it — opening a small PR to remove innerHTML uses and show escaped text. will push to canary in ~15m. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/492 jonah.s: we should also rotate admin session tokens / revoke active admin sessions. if an attacker triggered XSS they could exfiltrate session cookies. recommend invalidating all sessions created in last 48h and forcing reauth for admin roles. emily.ross: agreed. @nate.choi, can you run a session token invalidation job and confirm logs for any unexpected admin login locations? nate.choi: starting job now. will also grep auth logs for suspicious IPs and the fetch to attacker domain in web logs. maya.kapoor: initial check: we see two admin sessions with odd UA strings from same IP that accessed /admin/audit after those entries appeared. tagging for follow-up. sec_oncall_bot: Pager duty: oncall_security is paged. Please acknowledge. product-security: we need to prepare a comms plan if any customer data touched. preliminary: looks internal-to-admin UI but assume risk. start an internal timeline and list impacted customers just in case. frontend-eng: hotfix deployed to canary, rolling to prod in 5m. it replaces `el.innerHTML = entry.role_description` with `el.textContent = entry.role_description` and adds a sanitizer fallback. nate.choi: job finished: invalidated ~42 admin sessions, no evidence of mass token theft. found one outbound request to https://attacker.example/p?c=... from 2026-04-24T14:23:10 UTC from host admin-web-3. saving request raw headers. emily.ross: good. next: scrub rendered content from the UI (remove entries or mask role_description for now), and rotate any API keys that could have been exposed via cookies or local storage. product-security, do we need to involve legal? product-security: looped in privacy/legal for review. we should assume possibility of token exposure until proven otherwise. compile affected internal users and integrations. maya.kapoor: quick containment checklist I ran: 1) disable HTML rendering (done), 2) invalidate admin sessions (done), 3) take DB snapshot for forensic copy (in progress), 4) add a WAF rule to block attacker domain and known PoC patterns (nate please) nate.choi: WAF rule created to block requests containing `onerror=` payload patterns and visits to attacker.example. Also blocked IP seen in logs. jonah.s: long-term fixes: 1) input validation + escaping for all audit render paths, 2) CSP header for admin console (strict), 3) a unit/integration test that inserts typical attack payloads into audit entries and asserts no script execution, 4) add an export-scrub tool to redact HTML from history if needed. emily.ross: assign owners and deadlines. I'll own the postmortem and remediation tracking. @frontend-eng to get escaping and tests in by EOD. @nate.choi to finish forensic logs and WAF tuning by EOD. @product-security to draft internal comms and coordinate legal. sec_oncall_bot: Update: INC-2026-042 status -> containment achieved. Postmortem scheduled. maya.kapoor: follow-ups: check integrations that write role_description (service accounts, third-party connectors) — add server-side sanitization. also audit other admin UIs for similar innerHTML usages. product-security: I'll prepare an internal blameless summary and a short customer note template if needed. also will check compliance implications for audit log integrity (we may need to flag that logs were rendered but not modified). nate.choi: evidence so far suggests no escalation beyond XSS render and one exfil attempt. KMS keys not involved; no KMS access patterns anomalous. will include KMS check in final report. emily.ross: thanks everyone. immediate action items tracked in the incident doc: https://redwood-internal/ops/incidents/INC-2026-042 maya.kapoor: will follow up tomorrow with remediation PR numbers and a list of affected audit entries to scrub/mask. frontend-eng: deployed prod hotfix at 2026-04-24T15:02:00 UTC. will open follow-up PR to add CSP and tests. product-security: closing loop with legal/privacy once they've reviewed — tagging for follow-up meeting 2026-04-25 10:00 UTC. maya.kapoor: final note: great response. recommend adding a monitoring alert on rendered HTML tokens in admin UI to catch regressions. :thumbsup:
